title: European Pear: Ancient Pear Trees You Can Visit
meta_description: The oldest pear in the Netherlands has been feeding an almshouse jelly pot since 1638. Four old European pears mapped, in four countries.
intro: Nobody planted these to be looked at. A pear is an orchard tree, grown for fruit and replaced when it stops giving any, which is why four old ones spread across four countries is an odd list to be able to make. The oldest is in The Hague, planted in 1638 in the courtyard of an almshouse for women of unblemished character, and the residents have been turning its hard little juttepeers into jelly for something close to four centuries. Helsinki's is the last survivor of a manor orchard and is reckoned the tallest and oldest pear in Finland. Prague's, at around 190 years, stands where a demolished barracks once held the birthplace of the poet Jan Neruda. Warsaw's carries a name and an 1870 planting date that historians have taken apart piece by piece, and the tree keeps the name regardless.
